### 41.4 What only the headset shows

- The lines for a real player: 28 cm down for 0.15 s may be too shallow (a deep look at the floor, picking up a herb)
  or too deep for a short player; the hysteresis of 10 cm; the 0.5 s minimum.
- The cue's strength (0.3, 40 ms) and whether the dagger appearing in the right hand is a welcome sign of stealth or
  in the way (with the sword drawn the sword stays: SLOTS).
- Stealth itself: detection, the stealth-kill prompts (the band shows the game's prompts; `PromptOverrides
  'StealthMode'`), the Nemesis verbs' stealth kill from behind while ducked. Not seen headless.
- Not tried: sprinting while ducked, the bow drawn while ducked (`PC_WraithRanged_FromStealth` exists), a duck on a
  wall top or a ledge, a long crouch (HL:A's complaint: the button latch is the way out).

## 42. Front-first enemies: the fight circle's attacker choice, its timeline, the spawner, the damage path (static RE for build 14, 2026-10-26)

HG-5 and SH-9 (design-hla.md 2.10, 3.1, 3.2; design-vr.md "Turn-taking, difficulty, feedback"). The user holds the port
to HL:A and named "the places enemies spawn in relation to you, the warnings you get from enemies". The flat game picks
attackers from all around Talion because its orbit camera shows all of them; in VR the player sees about 100 deg.
`SOMVR_THREAT` (section 18) only warns about attacks the game has already started (0.8 s before an infantry impact:
`LATE`). This section is static RE in the som-linux Ghidra project; **no game boot**. It covers who may attack and
how the flat camera enters that choice, how long the commit -> impact takes, where arrivals are placed, and the damage
path at Talion. Built from it: the pure module `somvr_front.c` (tests/test_front.c, 92 checks; **not hooked into the
game**). 42.9 is build 14's design.

### 42.1 The call graph (the fight circle = `AICombatMgr`, instance `*0x463e290`)

```
CGameServerShell::vf_10 -> FUN_02997c80 -> FUN_028d97a0 (the manager's tick: FUN_028d5980, FUN_028d9030, FUN_028d0090,
                                                         FUN_028d7030 debug drawing, FUN_028d6a40, ...)
  -> FUN_028d7b50(target entry)            one call per target (Talion, and anyone else the AI fights)
       per slot (target+0x40 .. +0x48, 0xb8 bytes each):
         collect up to 32 candidates (target+0x28 list; entry = node - 0x10)
         only if no candidate holds a grant, the slot is armed (+0xb0) and its time has come (+0xa8 < now):
         for each: AICombatMgr_ScoreAttacker(entry, target, slot, n, best ring)   <- 0x28d7d31, its only call
         N = random(min, max) of the slot record (x2 on DoubleAttackChance: FUN_021189a0)
         sort by entry+0x20c (FUN_028d9e60 / FUN_028d9b20, comparator FUN_028ca050)
         grant the first N: FUN_028cd4b0(entry, now)                              <- 0x28d8295, its only call
           stop at the first negative score
FUN_028cd4b0 -> FUN_029ac220(orc): orc+0xc78 (its AI) +0x690 = 1 (may attack), +0x401 = 1 (re-plan)
  -> the AI: (anonymous)::DetermineFightCircleAttackerSubject::vf_02 (0x2a6ebe0) reads +0x690; the approach and the
     attack action -> Combat_StartAttack -> AICombatMgr_OnStartAttack (FUN_028d0ef0)
       attacks left (entry+0x22c) - 1; 0 -> FUN_028ccbc0 release (entry+0x214 = 0, ai+0x690 = 0: FUN_029ac260);
       else entry+0x214 = now (the grant renewed for the next attack of the streak)
  -> APPLYDAMAGE (the impact) -> Combat_DealHit -> ServerCombat_ApplyAttackDamage -> FUN_02810e80 -> DoDamage (42.7)
  -> the slot re-armed: FUN_028d6ef0 (42.5)
```

`AICombatMgr_ShouldCancelAttack` (`FUN_028d50c0`, 13 reasons) and `FUN_028d0990` (it adds an attacker that started an
attack without a grant: OnStartAttack's "OnStartAttack %s hit %s") are the other entries into the grant state.

### 42.2 The structures (offsets from the code above; **[high]** for the reads and writes, the names are ours)

- **The clock:** `*(uint32*)(*(*(0x463e290) + 0x8) + 0x14)` = the fight circle's time in ms (the grant's log prints it
  x 0.001 = `0x33becb0`; the lockouts add seconds x 1000 = `0x3347360`).
- **Target entry** (FUN_028d7b50's argument; the score's 2nd): `+0x28/+0x30` the attacker list; `+0x40/+0x48` the
  slots; `+0x70` the target's HOBJECT (the score's camera term tests its class list `+0x48` for `0x4c47040` and then
  takes `+0x38` = the `CPlayerObj`: the same test tells "this target is Talion"); `+0xa8` the state attacker lock
  ("State Attacker lock is set, and it's not us"); `+0xd0` the target's combat state record (`AICombatMgr_OnPreDeath`
  `FUN_028ccc90` sets it); `+0xe0` a timer; `+0xfc`, `+0xfd` flags.
- **Slot** (0xb8 bytes): `+0x80` a list; `+0x90` the last attacker's HOBJECT (the LastAttacker term); `+0x98` its
  record (the grant count's attributes `0x4ba0440+0xf8` min / `+0x128` max, the double-attack flag `+0x188`); `+0xa8`
  the next grant's time (ms); `+0xac` the lockout (s); `+0xb0` armed; `+0xb1` the lockout is scaled by
  `AttackDelayScalar`; `+0xb2` a pair granted.
- **Attacker entry** (the score's 1st argument): `+0x180` the orc (a server character: `+0x8` its HOBJECT, `+0xd2c`
  its world position in cm, `+0xc78` its AI); `+0x1a0` its target's HOBJECT; `+0x1f8` its AI combat record (rings,
  priority, attack counts `0x4b9f620+0x308/+0x338`); `+0x200` the slot record (0 = "Not using fight circle"); `+0x208`
  the distance (cm); **`+0x20c` the score**; **`+0x214` the grant's time (ms, 0 = none)**; `+0x220` BuffScore;
  `+0x224` a timer; `+0x22c` attacks left in the grant; `+0x22e` its ring (1 Inner, 2 Middle, 3 Outer, 4 Special);
  `+0x231` has a path, `+0x232` sees the target, `+0x233` LOS (`+0x234` LOS needed); `+0x236`, `+0x23a` "Can Be
  Attacker"; `+0x237` the pairing flag.

### 42.3 The score (`AICombatMgr_ScoreAttacker`, `0x28cd7a0`)

- **Rejections** write a negative code and return: not an AI -7, Can Be Attacker = FALSE -100, the target's class
  not a fighter -2, not using the fight circle -3, too far -4 (max 2000 cm + the record's extra), a ring not allowed
  -5 / -6 (Special) / -7 (None), Only Attacker / State Attacker lock -100, target not visible -16, no path -8, no LOS
  -9, no combat object -10, in a combat state -11, an attack that prevents selection -11.5, an aligned sync attack -12,
  attack + node -13, cannot engage -14, AlarmLevelChanger -15 (the veto's -50 is none of them).
- **Accepted** (`0x28ce56d..0x28ce5ae`): `Total = Distance + Priority + Camera + LastAttacker + StateScore + BuffScore`,
  at least 0.01 (`0x33f8d40`). Distance = weight x (max - distance) / max; Priority from the orc's record
  (`0x4b9f620+0x3c8`); LastAttacker when the slot's last attacker is this orc; StateScore when it is the target's
  locked attacker; BuffScore `entry+0x220`. The weights are attributes of the fight circle's record (`entry+0x200` ->
  `0x4ba0440+200` -> a record; attributes `0x4b9fde0+0x8` distance, `+0x38` on screen, `+0x68` off screen, `+0x98`
  last attacker); every default is 1.0 (`0x3344770`). **The values are DB data: runtime-unknown.**
- **The camera term** (`0x28ce488..0x28cebdd`): only when the target is the player (the class test above).
  `FUN_029a8130(orc+0xd2c, CPlayerObj)` = the frustum test `FUN_0229e170(point, {fov h, fov v}, pose)` with the copy's
  second pose `+0xbb0` and its FOVs `+0xbcc/+0xbd0` (full angles in radians: `tanf(0.5 x fov)`, the point projected to
  [0,1]^2 and in front). Off screen: **Camera = -w_off**. On screen: `CPlayerObj::vf_59` (vtbl+0x1d8) returns
  {pos, quat}, and Camera = w_on x cos(the angle between R(q)(0,0,1) and the direction pos -> orc) when that is > 0,
  else 0 (also 0 within 0.32 cm, the `0x3360530` guard). So at weight 1 an orc on screen in the middle scores up to 2
  more than one off screen: about two orcs' worth of distance term.
- **The pick:** the comparator (`FUN_028ca050(a, b)`, "a first") puts an entry with `+0x23a` set **and** its timer
  `+0x224` run out (`FUN_02390cb0`: `*(uint32*)timer < now`) before every other entry, whatever the scores. After
  that it sorts by Total, then by address. A negative score is never granted and the loop stops at the first one, so
  **a veto = a negative `entry+0x20c` written after the score call**. Nothing else in the pass reads the parts.
  **The trap:** a vetoed prio entry (`+0x23a`, timer run out) sorts first and ends the loop before an accepted orc in
  view is reached. While it stays vetoed, nobody gets the slot. So `somvr_front` warns a prio orc at once (an orc in
  view, `max_warn` and its quiet time do not hold it back), and the slot waits at most `warn_s` for it. The grant
  re-sets that timer (`FUN_02390c50(entry+0x224, s)`, s = the orc record's attribute `0x4b9f620+0x158`). The timer API is `FUN_02390c50` set
  (now + s x 1000), `FUN_02390cb0` run out, `FUN_02390ca0` clear, `FUN_02390cd0` set and run out.
- The game's own log of all this: the console variables `Combat.Debug.AttackerSelection` (the score's bool
  `0x4c44458`: "Rejected - ..." / "Accepted - Total = ..; Distance = .., Priority = .., Camera = .., ...") and
  `Combat.Debug.AIMgr` (`0x4c444d8`: "Can Attack: TRUE, score = .., %d attacks, at time ..", "received
  OnStartAttack"), with `Combat.Value.LogFileName` (re-gameplay.md 4 and 8 (a)).

### 42.4 The AI's camera copy (`CPlayerObj+0xb94..+0xbd3`) and who reads it

`FUN_027aa490(CPlayerObj*, P)` copies from the client player P (`P+0x2d0` = the camera object): `+0xb94` pos = the
camera's `+0x44c` (what `Player.GetPos` prints: Talion's position, not the orbit camera's), `+0xba0` quat (x y z w) =
`cam+0x458 (x) cam+0x484` (the effective camera rotation, the minimap's), `+0xbb0` / `+0xbbc` the same pose again,
`+0xbcc` / `+0xbd0` the FOVs (`cam+0x3fc` / `+0x400`, clamped). Called at `0x27add66` (in `FUN_027adc60`, which has no
static caller: a callback) and `0x27b6dd6` (in `CPlayerObj::vf_100`). The second call is reached every time `vf_100`
runs with the client player present (`FUN_02693910`) and `CPlayerObj+0xd12` clear. Slot 100 is overridden by
`CCharacter`, `NPC` and `CPlayerObj`, and the player's calls `CCharacter::vf_100`: probably the per-frame update
**[med]**. Readers:

| Reader | Via | What it decides |
|---|---|---|
| `AICombatMgr_ScoreAttacker` | `vf_59` (slot `0x3995b78`), `FUN_029a8130` | the Camera term (42.3) |
| `FUN_02258550` (attack-pool predicate) | `FUN_029a80d0` | an attack that wants its attacker on screen or off it (the pools' `AttackerOnScreen` / `MustBeOffScreen`) |
| `FUN_028f54b0` (the ambient spawner's point test) | `FUN_029a8130` | "Offscreen Predicate failure": spawns go off screen |
| `CAIGoalDespawnOffscreen::vf_09`, `FUN_028ba6a0` | `FUN_029a8180` | AI despawned off screen |
| `FUN_027982d0` (from `FUN_02798ae0`, `FUN_02799c30`, `FUN_02799e90`) | `FUN_029a8130` | not traced |

**In VR the copy is wrong.** The rotation is the game camera's, and with `SOMVR_YAW=camera` that is the rig's heading
(somvr_eyes.h), not where the player looks. So the Camera term, the on/off-screen attacks, the off-screen spawns and
the despawns all rate the play space's forward. Writing the head's pose and the headset's FOV into the copy after
`FUN_027aa490` (G2 for the AI only; the renderer's camera untouched) makes every reader above use the head. That is
the right meaning for all of them: "on screen" = in the headset.

### 42.5 The timeline (commit -> impact)

1. **A pass** runs in every manager tick while no candidate of the slot holds a grant, the slot is armed and
   `slot+0xa8 < now`. While every candidate is vetoed, nothing is granted. A pass without a grant writes only
   `slot+0xb2` (the pair flag), never its gate (`+0xa8`, `+0xb0`), so the pass runs again on the next tick **[high:
   the writes on that path]**.
2. **The grant** (`FUN_028cd4b0(entry, now)`): `+0x214 = now`, `+0x22c` = random(min, max) attacks, the AI flag.
3. **The attack start:** the AI's plan sees `ai+0x690`, approaches and starts an attack. The grant -> start latency is
   the AI's: **runtime-unknown**.
4. **The impact:** infantry 815 ms after the start, archers' release 2.6 s (P8, section 18.3).
5. **The re-arm** (`FUN_028d6ef0(slot)`: `+0xac` = 0.25 s (`0x4c4e1b0`) x `AttackDelayScalar` when `+0xb1`, `+0xa8 =
   now + 1000 x that`, `+0xb0 = 1`). The disarm (`FUN_028d6de0`, and `FUN_028cd340` from `FUN_026e7070`): `+0xac` =
   0.75 s (`0x4c4e1b4`) x `AttackDelayScalar`, `+0xb0 = 0`. Both have no static caller (callbacks: when they run is
   runtime-unknown). `AttackDelayScalar` is the difficulty manager's `+0x60` (`FUN_02118990`: `mulss 0x60(%rdi)`;
   `Difficulty_Recompute` `FUN_02114ec0` writes it); `DoubleAttackChance` is `+0x64` (`FUN_021189a0`). **The two base
   times are writable statics** set by `_INIT_1466` (`0x634d74`, `0x634d7e`), not console variables: build 14 can
   scale them once at start.

So with a veto before the grant, an attack from behind lands at the earliest **warn_s + the grant -> start latency +
0.815 s** after its warning starts (at least 1.8 s with warn_s 1.0). THREAT's own warning at the start stays on top.
A grant made while the orc was in view, after which the player turned away, is not vetoed. THREAT warns about it
(0.8 s); `ShouldCancelAttack` is the place to cancel it later, if needed.

### 42.6 Arrivals (SH-9): the spawner

`AISpawnMgr` is only the save chunk and the console (`SetLimit` empty, `DumpStats`). The spawning is the
`AISpawnerAmbient*` family:
- `AISpawnerAmbientBase::vf_32` (`0x28f98d0`, slot 32 of 8 spawner classes; the Gang, GangSimEvent, Nemesis, Normal
  and SimEvent spawners' own vf_32 call it) spawns.
- `FUN_028f54b0` tests each spawn point ("%s rejected - Offscreen Predicate failure (%s[%d])", "LOS Predicate
  failure"; `FUN_029a8130` with the camera copy).
- `FUN_028fb690` (called by `FUN_028fd460`) sets the new AI up and logs "[AI|SPAWNAMBIENT|CREATE]: %s Spawned an AI
  (%s); Template = %s; IsNamed = %s".

The game places arrivals off screen, which in the flat game means behind the orbit camera. With the copy from the
head, they are placed outside the headset's view. That is HL:A's rule: nothing pops in where you look.

**The cue needs no spawner hook:** every orc that joins the fight against Talion becomes a candidate in his target
entry, and the score wrapper sees it. The first time an orc is seen (a new HOBJECT) out of view within 15 m gets an
arrival cue (the positional sound and a marker, SH-9). THREAT's 40 m scan is the second source. A hook on the
spawner would also see spawns that never join a fight (for later, when the arrival marker needs the spawn moment
itself). `FUN_028fb690` is a devirtualised clone of `vf_32`: `FUN_028fd460` tests the spawner's slot 32 against
`0x28f98d0` and calls the clone directly (`0x28fd879`; RCX = the new AI, kept in R14 by its prologue). Otherwise it
calls the slot (`0x28fdf88`). The five derived spawners' own vf_32 call `0x28f98d0` (R8 = the new AI, also kept in R14).
So a complete spawn hook is this call plus those five calls (not taken):

```
SITE("FR_SPAWN", K_CALL, 0x28fd879, 0x28fd862, "48 8b 8d d0 fe ff ff 4d 89 e0 4c 89 fa 4c 89 ef 48 8b b5 f0 fe ff ff e8 12 de ff ff", 0x28fb690, "41 57 49 89 f7 41 56 49 89 ce 41 55 49 89 fd 41"),
```

### 42.7 The damage path at Talion (D10)

`Combat_DealHit` (`0x26d4ff0`), `Combat_ApplyDamageKey`, the collider hits, `FUN_02714410/0720`, ... ->
`ServerCombat_ApplyAttackDamage` (`0x281a200`, 8 callers) -> `FUN_02810e80(attacker, targetChar, .., ds)`. Its amount
is `ds+0x50`: < 0 is a heal (`FUN_02763910`); > 0 goes to **`DamageStruct_DoDamage(ds, targetChar[1] = the target's
HOBJECT)` at `0x2811007`**. `DoDamage` (`0x2763050`) checks the class and **tail-jumps at `0x2763094`** to
`FUN_00c77890(obj, damager, ds)` -> the object's damage handler (vtbl+0xc0). DoDamage has 18 callers (FragSelf,
props, sync actions, explosions, ...). So:
- `FR_DMG_ATK` (the call at `0x2811007`) = all attack damage (the orcs' blows; arrows if their hits carry an attack:
  **RT**);
- `FR_DMG_ALL` (the tail jump) = everything, scripted kills included.

The scale is applied when RSI (the target's HOBJECT) is Talion's and the amount is > 0, keeping amounts from
`keep_above` up (a scripted kill stays a kill: `somvr_front_damage`). SOMVR_HURT reads the health drop as before.

- Patched in build 14:
  - `FR_SCORE`: the veto. The original's arguments are RDI entry, RSI target, RDX slot, ECX the candidates, R8D the
    best ring; it returns void; R14/R10 are saved by the caller.
  - `FR_GRANT`: the warning used up, plus the grant log. ESI is the clock (`now`).
  - `FR_CAMCOPY_A/B`: the head into the copy, after the original.
  - `FR_DMG_ATK`: the damage scale.
- Read-only proofs:
  - `FR_CAMTERM`: the class test `0x4c47040`, `+0x38`, the orc's `+0x180 -> +0xd2c`, the vf_59 call;
  - `FR_VF59`: the copy's layout `+0xb94` / `+0xba4`;
  - `FR_REARM`: the clock `0x463e290` and the 0.25 s static at `0x4c4e1b0` (`f3 0f 10 05 9b 72 37 02` =
    `movss 0x237729b(%rip)`).
- `FR_DMG_ALL` is the alternative to `FR_DMG_ATK`. None of the nine is used by somvr or the probe today: no
  `EXCLUSIVE` entry needed.

### 42.9 Build 14: the design (not built; the pure part is `somvr_front.c`)

| Switch | Default | What |
|---|---|---|
| `SOMVR_FRONT=0\|1` | 0 | the veto (`FR_SCORE`, `FR_GRANT`); needs `SOMVR_THREAT` (the head pose, the warning cue) |
| `SOMVR_FRONT_VIEW_DEG` | `SOMVR_THREAT_VIEW_DEG` (110) | the in-view cone |
| `SOMVR_FRONT_WARN_S` | 1.0 | the warning before a grant from out of view (HG-5) |
| `SOMVR_FRONT_READY_S` / `_QUIET_S` | 2.0 / 2.0 | how long a finished warning lets the orc be granted / no new warning after an unused one |
| `SOMVR_FRONT_FAR_M` | 0 | out-of-view orcs farther than this are not vetoed (0 = all) |
| `SOMVR_FRONT_MAX_WARN` | 1 | warnings at a time |
| `SOMVR_FRONT_CAMCOPY=off\|head` | off | the AI's camera copy from the head (`FR_CAMCOPY_A/B`); `_FOV_H` / `_FOV_V` 110 / 90 deg |
| `SOMVR_FRONT_LOCKOUT` | 1.0 | x the slot's 0.25 s and 0.75 s (the two statics, written once at start; HG-5's tuning: 1.5) |
| `SOMVR_FRONT_DAMAGE` | 1.0 | x the damage at Talion (`FR_DMG_ATK`, patched only when < 1; D10: 0.5); `_KEEP` 1000 |

**The game side (`somvr_front_game.c`, a `FRONT_SITES` block, check_sites.py counting it):**
1. **`fr_score(e, tgt, slot, n, ring)`** calls the original first. Then, when on: the target is Talion (the class test
   on `tgt+0x70`, or its `+0x38` == his `CPlayerObj`), the head pose is fresh (THREAT's frame, at most 100 ms old;
   else fail open), the orc `o = *(e+0x180)`, id `*(o+8)`, its position `o+0xd2c`, then `somvr_th_local` /
   `somvr_th_direction` from the head, prio = `e+0x23a && *(uint32*)(e+0x224) < now`, `somvr_front_judge(pass =
   slot, now = the clock, ...)`, and the score written back to `e+0x20c`.
2. **A warning that starts** (`*started` / the frame's `somvr_front_end_pass`) becomes a THREAT track of a new kind
   `pre` for that orc before any attack: the warning sound at the orc (`SOMVR_THREAT_SOUND`), the edge on its side
   rising with `somvr_front_warn_level`, one announce pulse on that side's hand. The orc's weapon hand is read as for
   an attack. Its attack start then continues as the normal track, and is no longer `LATE`.
3. **`fr_grant(e, now)`** calls the original, then (`e+0x214 != 0`) `somvr_front_granted` and the log.
4. Once a frame (`th_frame`): `somvr_front_end_pass(the clock)`.
5. **`fr_camcopy(pl, P)`**: the original, then `somvr_front_camcopy_fill(the head, the head's quat, the FOVs)` written
   over `pl+0xb94..+0xbd3`. Paused, flat or third-person frames leave the game's copy.
6. **`fr_dmg(ds, hobj)`**: when hobj is Talion's, `ds+0x50 = somvr_front_damage(...)`, then the original.

A site mismatch turns that part off. With no `CPlayerObj`, no head or no record free, the game's own choice stands.

**Logs:**
- `CONFIG front on=1 view_deg=110 warn_s=1.0 ready_s=2.0 quiet_s=2.0 far_m=0 max_warn=1 camcopy=head fov=110x90
  lockout=1.50 damage=0.50; sites: FR_SCORE ok ...`;
- `FRONT veto orc=.. score=.. -> -50 off=.. deg dist=.. m` (the first 50, then at most 2 a second);
- `FRONT warn orc=.. side=L|R|LR yaw=.. dist=.. m (best of ..)`, `FRONT ready orc=.. after .. s`;
- `FRONT grant orc=.. verdict=in-view|ready|far|full|game attacks=.. warned .. s ago`;
- `FRONT expired orc=..`;
- `FRONT camcopy pos=.. fwd=.. (the game's fwd ..)` once a second;
- `FRONT damage at Talion ..->..`;
- the end counters (`somvr_front`'s).

**Headless proof** (headless_vr.sh, no headset; the same drivers as section 30's fights): the practice area
(`SOMVR_PRACTICE`, its one orc) plus a second orc (`fight spawn`, if the combat drivers allow two; else the practice's
"again"). The probe's console sets `Combat.Debug.AttackerSelection 1`, `Combat.Debug.AIMgr 1` and
`Combat.Value.LogFileName` to the run folder, so the game's own score lines sit next to ours.
- (a) The orc in front (the mock HMD looking at it): grants with verdict `in-view`, no `FRONT veto`, and the game's
  `Camera = +..` terms.
- (b) The scripted head turned 180 deg (the driver's head-yaw word) with the orc engaged: `FRONT veto`, one `FRONT
  warn`, `FRONT ready` >= 1.0 s later, then `FRONT grant ... ready`. THREAT's start for that orc follows, with the
  warning's start -> the impact >= 1.8 s and no `LATE`. The grant -> start latency is measured here (`FRONT grant` vs
  `THREAT start`).
- (c) `SOMVR_FRONT_CAMCOPY=head`: the game's `Camera = ..` follows the head (it flips sign with the 180 deg turn while
  the rig's heading stays). Spawns stay off view: the ambient spawner's "Offscreen Predicate" lines, if any.
- (d) `SOMVR_FRONT_DAMAGE=0.5`: `FIGHT hurt` / the health drop per blow halves.
- (e) 0 `WARN`, the install unchanged, the save unchanged.

**Runtime-unknown (what the boots must show):**
- the score weights (DB values) and typical totals;
- the grant -> start latency;
- how often `FUN_027aa490` runs (every `vf_100` with `+0xd12` clear: per frame?), which of its two calls is live,
  and what `+0xd12` is (a freeze in cinematics?);
- what the head copy changes for the other readers (spawns, despawns, the on/off-screen attack pools);
- whether arrows pass `FR_DMG_ATK`;
- when the re-arm and disarm run (they are callbacks);
- whether archers share the melee slots (a veto on an archer is probably wanted: arrows from behind get the warning
  too);
- that the AI tick runs on the game thread, where the head pose is cached.

### 42.10 Build 14 at runtime: `SOMVR_FRONT` hooked (2026-10-26, headless; handoff/HANDOFF-front.md)

**Built** (`somvr_front_game.c`, its `FRONT_SITES` block = 42.8's nine lines, check_sites.py counts it: 9 ok):

### 42.11 Round 2: THREAT's view by bearing, one warning per attack, bigger fights (2026-10-26, headless; handoff/HANDOFF-front.md "Round 2")

**Built** (branch of the threat14 helper; every switch below is in scripts/headset-build14.env's round 2 block):
- **One in-view test** (`somvr_th_view_off` / `somvr_th_in_view`, somvr_threat.c): THREAT's cues (attacks, the near
  cue, projectiles), FRONT's veto, its cue's "looked at" and its arrival watch all compare the same angle with
  `view_deg / 2`: the bearing, |yaw| in the head's frame, the pitch ignored (a point more than 85 deg above or below:
  the full angle, its yaw means nothing there). `SOMVR_THREAT_VIEW=bearing|full` (default bearing; full = round 1's
  THREAT, and FRONT follows it: one test). `CONFIG threat ... view=bearing keyless=0`.
- **THREAT judges an attack's view at the orc's body** (its root + 100 cm, `TH_BODY_UP_CM`), not at its weapon hand:
  with the bearing on the hand (run 092140) an orc fighting at Talion's feet in plain view still gave 4 `LATE` edge
  warnings in 21 s - at 1.2 m its hand swings 57-65 deg out to the side half a second before the blow. The glow stays
  on the hand; the edge's side is the body's.
- **Keyless attacks get no cue** (`SOMVR_THREAT_KEYLESS=0`, the default; 1 = round 1's): an attack record whose ten key
  times are all 0xffff (no impact, no parry window, no BCOL, no SHOOT). Run 092140, five orcs: **200 of 254 attack
  starts at Talion were keyless**, none of them a blow (220 ended replaced by the orc's next record after 1.44 s on
  average, 29 with the orc gone); THREAT announced each out of view with a pulse and the sound: **114 of its 148
  announcements**. They are the orcs' moves between blows (the walk-in after a grant, the circling); the real blows
  have their table (impact 0.80 s). The start line says `keyless: no cue`, `THREAT END ... keyless N: no cue`. FRONT's
  "the grant's attack" is now the first keyed track after the grant (round 1 could take a keyless move).
- **`SOMVR_FRONT_ONECUE=1` (default): one warning per attack from out of view.** For an attack FRONT warned about (its
  warning runs or is ready, or it is the first keyed attack the warned grant started within 2.5 s), THREAT's own pulse
  and sound are skipped when FRONT's warning gave them (`THREAT quiet orc=.. haptic=announce sound skipped: FRONT warned
  it .. s ago`); `LATE` is cleared as in round 1; the edge glow is held at the warning's end level (0.8 x the edge)
  from the grant to that attack's impact (on the track's own clock, which follows the orc's animation timer), and
  THREAT's edge rises over it in the last 0.8 s. So the player gets, per blow from behind: the sound at the orc and one
  pulse on its side 1.8 s before the impact, an edge glow on that side rising and staying until the blow, nothing
  else. 0 = round 1's. Per warned attack a `FRONT cues` line (pulses and sounds, the warning's and THREAT's, THREAT's
  skipped, the edge's span); `FRONT END ... warned attacks N (pulses x, max m, sounds y per attack; THREAT's skipped
  ...; edge held .. frames)`; `THREAT end ... pulses N sounds N`.
- FRONT's event lines (warn, ready, grant, attack, expired, prewarned) have their own log budget (400, then 20 a
  second): in round 1 the score lines used up the shared one and grants went unlogged in fights.

**Round 1's pulse count** (run 081743's log; one orc behind, `SOMVR_FRONT=1`): per blow the FRONT warning (pulse +
sound) 1 s before the grant, THREAT's announcement (pulse + sound, `LATE` cleared) at the attack's start, its urgent
pulse 0.35 s before the impact: **3 pulses and 2 sounds within 1.8 s for one blow**, plus a pulse and the sound for
every keyless move out of view. Run 092140 (five orcs, 3.5 min of fighting, keyless still cued): **305 pulses, 179
sounds**. Not HL:A's one readable cue.

**Runs** (logs/boot-check-20261026-*; scripts/threat14-drive.sh: `feet` = one orc spawned 2 m ahead, fighting at
Talion's feet with the head forward, then turned 180 deg; `crowd` = five orcs kept, the head forward, a sweep of 3 s
turns, behind, to the side; every run 0 WARN, the install unchanged, the save UNCHANGED):
- **092140** (build 14's env + `view=bearing`, `ONECUE=1`; the hand point, keyless cued): feet-front 4 `LATE` edges
  (the hand 57-65 deg out); the crowd 29-62 THREAT announcements per phase; totals 305 pulses, 179 sounds.
- **093343** (+ the body point, keyless no cue): **feet-front: 0 THREAT warnings, 0 edge cues, 11 glows, 11 in-view
  grants** (the orc at Talion's feet straight ahead: 0.6 m, yaw +3); **behind: 12 FRONT warnings, 11 ready grants,
  every warned attack `pulses 1 (the warning's 1 + THREAT's 0), sounds 1 (1 + 0), THREAT's skipped 3`**, its warning
  1.00-1.05 s before the start and 1.80-1.85 s before the impact. Totals **40 pulses (305 in 092140), 28 sounds (179)**
  for about the same fight (419 vs 437 attack starts, 81 vs 82 grants), keyless 343 of 419. The THREAT warnings left (7
  `LATE`) are orcs granted in view whose blow started out of view (they had circled to 55-65 deg): real blows without a
  warning, announced as before. The edge hold ran 1 frame there (it matched the track by its start time, which follows
  the orc's timer): fixed by the start's serial (cf69572).
- **095005** (`all` + `_MAX_WARN=2`; the hold fixed): the edge held to the impact (`the edge 0.00..1.80 s after the
  warning's start`, 16-17 held frames); 33 warned attacks, 1.03 pulses and 1.00 sounds each (the one with 2: its
  warning was looked at before its cue, so THREAT's own pulses ran); feet-front had 4 FRONT warnings because that orc
  fought at Talion's right shoulder (yaw 65-80 deg at 0.3-0.5 m: out of the headset's view, rightly warned). Totals 68
  pulses, 46 sounds (more warnings: 44).
- **095712** (`crowd`, the env as is: `_MAX_WARN=1`, `_LOCKOUT=1.0`, all events logged): 21 pulses, 13 sounds, keyless
  340 of 390 starts.
- **100322** (`crowd` + `_LOCKOUT=1.5`: the statics 0.375 / 1.125 s written): 33 pulses, 23 sounds; 11 warned attacks,
  1 pulse and 1 sound each.

**Bigger fights** (five orcs, infantry and shields, kept with `front keep 1`; the head forward, swept in 3 s turns,
behind, to the side; the crowd window of each run, from scripts/threat14-drive.sh's PHASE lines and the grant lines):

| run | switches | grants at Talion | per s | max gap | orcs granted | warnings (2 at once) | ready grants |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 095712 | `_MAX_WARN=1`, `_LOCKOUT=1.0` | 48 in 116 s | 0.41 | 4.1 s | 5 (18/14/12/3/1) | 6 (0) | 1 |
| 095005 | `_MAX_WARN=2` | 45 in 117 s | 0.38 | 4.0 s | 3 (27/10/8) | 20 (10) | 6 |
| 100322 | `_LOCKOUT=1.5` | 44 in 115 s | 0.38 | 4.4 s | 3 (20/13/11) | 17 (0) | 10 |

- **The fight flows**: a grant at Talion every 2.4-2.6 s, no gap over 4.4 s, every grant an attack, no stuck slot. The
  game keeps 2-3 orcs in its inner ring and rejects the middle ring's (-5, "ring not allowed": `verdict=game ring=2`
  in `front status`): its own pacing, the veto does not hold the fight up.
- **The "sorted first" trap** (entry+0x23a with its +0x224 timer run out): 0 prio candidates in all six runs.
- **`_MAX_WARN=2`**: two orcs behind warned at once (10 times), more of them attack after a warning (6 ready grants vs
  1), the same pace (0.38/s vs 0.41/s); the player then gets two edges and two pulses at once. Kept at 1 (front first:
  the orcs in view take the turns, one warning at a time).
- **`_LOCKOUT=1.5`**: no clear change (0.38/s vs 0.41/s, max gap 4.4 vs 4.1 s): the attack's own length paces the slot,
  as with one orc in round 1. Kept at 1.0.
- The samples are small (one run each): which orcs stand in the inner ring and where the head points decide more than
  the switches (095712's crowd-behind had no warning at all: the orcs had circled into the turned view; 100322's had 10).

**Do keyless records ever hurt?** Run **102136** (`all` + `SOMVR_FRONT_DAMAGE=0.99`: the damage hook in, 21 -> 20.79,
every hit at Talion logged with the attacker's THREAT track at that moment, `FRONT damage ... its track: keyed at ..
s (impact .. s) | KEYLESS at .. s | none`): **106 hits, all from a keyed track, 0 keyless, 0 none** (362 of 440 starts
keyless). The hits land at the track's impact (74 within -0.1..+0.05 s), 26 at +0.2..+0.5 s, 3 at +2.5..+4.9 s (the same
keyed track still on). Round 1's logs suggested otherwise (9 of 70 hits in 082352 had a keyless last start for the
attacker), but those lines had no time and the track map was the grant's: the live track at the hit says keyed. The
feet plan there: 2 THREAT warnings for the orc in front, at yaw -55..-57 (the cone's edge at 1.2 m, judged in view by
FRONT a moment before); behind, 20 warned attacks, 1 pulse and 1 sound each; the crowd 0.40 grants/s, max gap 3.9 s.

**Not proven:** the headset (one pulse + one sound + a held edge per blow from behind: readable? 1.8 s at 90 Hz?);
the bearing's blind spot (the head pitched steeply: an orc ahead counts as seen; the test head only turns); THREAT's own
unwarned attacks keep their two pulses (announce, urgent); hits up to 0.5 s after THREAT's impact estimate (26 of 106 in
102136) make its urgent pulse early for those; an orc at the cone's edge (55-67 deg at ~1 m) flickers between seen and
warned (no hysteresis).

### 43.1 Where the story is on the save (the probe's navdump, P7)

### 43.2 The pad's bindings at story moments (`USE bindings`, the game's binding table per pad button)
| Where | A | B | RB |
|---|---|---|---|
| the world | - | - | Activate 34, CombatSecondary02 123, QuestConfirm 282 |
| a mission card (a presentation, `ctx=world`) | QuestConfirmStart 283 | QuestConfirmCancel 284 | - |
| a failed mission (a presentation, `ctx=world`) | QuestFailedRetry 285 | QuestFailedAbandon 286 | - |

QuestConfirm 282 is active in the world everywhere (the stock RB presses it with every Activate); at a marker it opens
the card. 283 pressed at a Nemesis marker without the card started the mission at once (run 081246). Nothing skip-like
(CinematicSkip 260/261, SkipPresentations 265) is bound during a captain's introduction.

### 43.3 The flow
- A marker: "<mission> — [RB] Start Mission" on the HUD (top right in the flat game; not a PromptShow diamond, so
  SOMVR_PAD_PROMPTS never sees it). 282 -> the card: BODYMOMENT `cond - -> pres`, `window 0 -> 1 by pres (flat frames:
  the menu quad)` while `SESSION ui` stays `ctx=world paused=0` - the controllers are not the pad there (3.5). The
  card shows the mission's picture and line and "(A) Accept (B) Cancel".
- 283 -> 0.3 s of the game's black cover (SOMVR_XR_COVER: the loading space 1.8 s) -> a load -> for the story mission
  a video: `SESSION ui ... video=1 ctx=menu` for 102 s (the game re-creates its 1920 x 1080 swapchain at the video's
  start and end); two presses about 1 s apart skip it (MenuEnter, then MenuEscape: run 083012 at 56 s), 10 s apart do
  not -> the cover -> the world with a timed objective ("01:30 Make haste to the Sea Fort while avoiding detection").
  For the Nemesis mission: the card, 283, the cover, then the captain's introduction: `pres` 4-5 s in the window
  (Ratlûg's name and line).
- **The story video's presents are layout-B frames without eye images** (`the tag says eyes 0x0`): build 13's layer
  showed the last stereo frame again for all of them (`reuse 600`: a frozen world). `SOMVR_XR_THEATRE_VIDEO=on` makes
  them mono frames while the session says a video: the video on the theatre's 5 m screen (`theatre 3: a video on a
  5.0 m screen at +0.09,+0.00,-4.98`, run 091332).
- Failing: leaving the area ("Too far from Mission!") or the timer ("Out of Time! Hint: Use the Elven Swiftness
  ability") -> a presentation in the window, the game's third-person shot of Talion, "(A) Retry (B) Abandon"; 286 ->
  "Leave Mission — Are you sure ...? (A) Yes (B) No" as a real pause (`paused=1 ctx=menu`: the menu passthrough).
- The theatre at runtime: a load on 2.4 m at 2.4 m, the window on 3 m at 3 m, a video on 5 m at 5 m (with the fix).
  Build 13 placed a kind once (`KA.th_kind` was reset on mono frames only): the next window of that kind reused the
  first one's place; `SOMVR_XR_THEATRE_RESEAT=on` places each new one where the head faces (`(reseat: placed again

giver's prompt, a door or lever's Activate prompt.

### 43.7 "[RB] Start Mission": where its glyph comes from (static, som-linux)
The marker's line is CUIHUDQuestConfirm (`SQuestConfirmData`, CUIHUDEventManager::OnQuestShowConfirmation):
FUN_00f56820 goes to the movie's "Confirm" frame and sets the StringId `UI_QuestConfirm_Confirm` ("Start Mission";
`UI_TravelPoint_Confirm` for a fast-travel tower, `UI_QuestConfirm_InCombat` in a fight). It asks no binding: the
binding lookup FUN_00aaaf50 (which the prompt diamonds' glyphs come from, 43.4) is called by the prompt diamonds,
CStrugglePressCount / CStruggleAim's widgets (FUN_00ecbe40 / FUN_00ecfe00: an icon by command) and a few others, none
in the quest HUD. So the RB is the movie's own picture: SOMVR_PAD_PROMPTS' relabel cannot reach it, and changing it
means the movie (not done). The Controls page names B for it instead (43.10).

## 44. The story's way-finding: the objective marker in the world, the Sea Fort's 1:30 (build 15 candidate, 2026-10-26)
handoff/HANDOFF-objective.md (the runs, the pictures); scripts/objective15-drive.sh. Build 14's switches
(scripts/headset-build15.env) plus `SOMVR_OBJECTIVE` (default off). Section 43 is the story drill's, 45 the
collectibles' helper's.

### 44.1 Where the game places its objective marker (static, som-linux; re-hud.md 3, re-ui-effects.md 2)
The HUD's objective "coin" is a nav marker (`CNavMarkerInstance`, the list `0x46b9200`) like every other world icon.
`FUN_00ec4f10(player)` walks the list once per view and calls **`FUN_00ec4a50(marker, player)` at `0xec4f83`**:
the marker's world position `FUN_00ebc700(m, &pos)` (-> bool), the distance from the player `FUN_00ad1610(P)` / 100,
the record's range `FUN_00ebced0(m)` (-> {min, max} m packed in xmm0; default {0, 100}: hidden outside it), then the
projection **`FUN_00a60920(*(P+0x2d0) = the player camera, &pos, &onScreen, &behind)` at `0xec4d7f`** (the camera
object's transform and `cam+0x404` = tan of its half FOVs: the flat 43.1 x 25.0 deg camera, not the eyes), the UI
rect, then `FUN_00ec2660` (on screen) or `FUN_00ec3900` (the edge arrow, `RenderOffScreen`); not placed = the hide:
`m+0x45 = 0`, `m+0x6d = 0`, `clip = *(m+0xb0)`, `clip->vtbl[0x208/8](clip, 0)`. The caller ignores the return value.
In VR the HUD is one quad 1.5 m ahead, so the coin (placed by the camera, not the head) sat at the quad's edge with an
arrow whatever the head did (43.6).

### 44.2 The design: our own marker, the game's place (`SOMVR_OBJECTIVE=on`)
Re-projecting the coin into the HUD quad through the head was rejected: the quad is world-locked and 44 x 25 deg, so
an objective beside or behind the player has no place on it, and the coin would sit at panel depth. Instead (G19's
"capture and re-draw"):
- **OB_EACH** (K_CALL `0xec4f83`, a stub page, `bo_patch_call`): the original, then for a marker whose record name
  matches `SOMVR_OBJECTIVE_RECS` (default `Objective*`) its world position (OB_POS, every call: it may move with its
  target) and the game's own tests before the projection (active `+0x2e0`, enabled `+0x2e1`, a position, within
  OB_RANGE of Talion's root: "eligible"). In our stereo frames (`g_fr.on`) the game's icon is hidden by the game's own
  hide (above). Every marker the game shows is logged at first sight (`OBJECTIVE t=.. marker N m=.. 'NAME' ...`).
  Record names and matches are cached by record pointer (open addressing); the hook costs a few loads per marker.
- After the frame's body (H4, `ob_frame`): the nearest eligible objective seen this frame goes into the ninth
  exported object **`somvr_objective`** ("SOMROBJ1" v1, 392 bytes, `somvr_objective.h`): per stereo frame (keyed by
  the record's frame id, as `somvr_threat`) its place in the layer's reference space (the frame's own rig:
  `somvr_th_to_xr`) and its distance from Talion (the text). Paused, no player: n = 0.
- **The layer** (`vklayer/somvr_objective_layer.c`, slot `XL_OBJ` over the ring and under the HUD; the first to go
  after the menu backdrop when a frame would carry more layers than the runtime takes): `somvr_ob_locate` (pure,
  somvr_objective.c) against the frame's head (the eyes' middle, the left eye's orientation) and the views' union fov:
  - **in view** (its tangents within 0.80 of the view's edges; it stays in until 0.90): a 4 deg square world-locked
    on the head -> objective line at the objective's distance up to 12 m (never under 2 m; none nearer than 3 m:
    Talion is there), billboarded to the head, shifted so the diamond (0.31 of the cell from its top), not the cell's
    centre, sits on the direction; within 5 deg of the view's centre the faint copy (40 %) so it never covers what is
    looked at;
  - **out of view**: a 5 deg arrow in a VIEW space 1 m ahead on the ellipse at 0.72 of the view's tangents, parallel
    to the view's plane (undistorted), rolled to the objective's way in the view (behind: the nearer side).
  - The picture (390 x 130: the diamond with the distance, its faint copy, the arrow; premultiplied) is drawn by
    `somvr_ob_image` (the menu's VGA font at 2x, a dark rim) when the distance's text changes ("236 m", "1.2 km") and
    uploaded into the next image of an ordinary swapchain (one staging buffer, its fence waited before the next write).
    A reuse frame repeats the last quad. A dumped frame writes `<log>.objectiveN.ppm` (+ `.alpha.pgm`): xr_compose.py
    draws it (the arrow mapped from its VIEW space).
- Nothing moves, nothing is pressed; the game's own data decides what is shown and where.

### 44.3 Switches, words, lines
- `SOMVR_OBJECTIVE=off|log|on|both` (default off): log = the hook logs, nothing hidden or published; on = our marker,
  the game's icon hidden in our stereo frames; both = our marker and the game's icon. `SOMVR_OBJECTIVE_RECS` (default
  `Objective*`; `,` between patterns, a trailing `*`), `SOMVR_OBJECTIVE_SIZE_DEG` (4), `_DIST_M` (12), `_FAINT_DEG` (5),
  `_EDGE_DEG` (5). Layer: `SOMVR_XR_OBJECTIVE=on|off` (default on: draws only with an active `somvr_objective`).
- Words: `objective status` (the counts and every marker seen in the last 5 s: place, eligible, hidden),
  `objective on|game|both` (live), `objective recs PATTERNS`.
- Lines: `OBJECTIVE site ...`, `HOOK OB_EACH ok ...`, `CONFIG objective=...`, `OBJECTIVE t=.. marker N ...` (first
  sight), `OBJECTIVE t=.. frame=..: the marker in the eyes: 'NAME'` / `no objective in the eyes`, every 5 s `OBJECTIVE
  t=.. 'NAME' marker N at (...), D m from Talion ...; xr (...) m; the game's icon placed (hidden by us); layer: marker
  frames, edge frames`, `OBJECTIVE END ...`; layer `xr: objective: somvr_objective found ...`, `xr: objective frame N:
  ... -> the marker world-locked | the faint marker world-locked | the edge arrow head-locked at ... (frames ...)` on
  each change, `xr: objective: the arrow points D deg`, `xr: objective: picture N ('236 m') uploaded`, `xr: dump
  objective frame N`.
- Sites (the OBJECTIVE_SITES block of somvr_objective_game.c; check_sites.py 3/3 ok, byte proofs against the binary):
```c
SITE("OB_EACH", K_CALL, 0xec4f83, 0xec4f70, "48 89 dd 4c 8b 63 08 48 83 c5 80 74 2a 4c 89 ee 48 89 ef e8 c8 fa ff ff", 0xec4a50, "41 57 41 56 41 55 41 54 49 89 fc 55 53 48 89"),
SITE("OB_POS", K_ENTRY, 0xebc700, 0xebc700, "48 8b 87 50 02 00 00 48 85 c0 74 0f 48 89 c7 48", 0xebc700, "48 8b 87 50 02 00 00 48 85 c0 74 0f 48 89 c7"),
SITE("OB_RANGE", K_ENTRY, 0xebced0, 0xebced0, "55 53 48 83 ec 28 48 8b 1d 43 a0 ca 03 48 8b af", 0xebced0, "55 53 48 83 ec 28 48 8b 1d 43 a0 ca 03 48 8b"),
```
- Tests: tests/test_objective.c (39: the patterns, the text, ahead / near / too near, the hysteresis, the edges right,
  left, up, behind on either side, the arrow's axis, a NaN head, the ABI's entry, the picture's cells, guards, faint copy
  and arrow); test_layer `objective` (none, ahead with its picture byte for byte, the same text not uploaded again, a new
  text, the edge arrow in a VIEW space, a reuse frame, gone, counters, teardown), `objective-absent`, `-inactive`, `-off`.

### 44.5 The Sea Fort's 1:30 (task 2's answer)
- "Make haste to the Sea Fort" is **two waypoints of the same 'Objective' record**: wp1, its marker at 23434 1758 -8684
  (234 m from the golden M, 20 m lower) but **completed in a region at the valley floor below the second edge** (the
  marker switched with Talion at 28286 -14237 and 28455 -14407, 75-80 m before that point), then **wp2 = the Sea
  Fort, its marker at 23100 2865 450** (the trigger there: the video). The HUD's coin and our marker follow the game's
  marker from one to the next. Round 2's "within 4 m of 'Objective' at 76-82 s with no completion, the coin 80-90 m on"
  was wp1 long done and the fort still ahead. The 1:30 starts with the marker (~5 s after the video) or at a Retry.
- Measured on the bot's own line (the sprint latch, A at the three edge cues): **start -> 26202 -11431 in 51.6 s**
  (131947 attempt 1) **+ 26202 -11431 -> the fort in 31.2 s** (134333, one continuous walk) = **82.8 s**, plus ~1 s
  from the Retry to the walk's start: **~84 s of the 90**. The bot's line is not the best one: after the valley drop
  (wp1 done at ~42 s) it ran on to wp1's marker point; the fort is 160 m straight from there (25 s at 6.4 m/s): a
  player who follows our marker to the fort is faster if the way is open (not walked). So a VR player with the sprint
  latch and A at the edges makes it with some 6 s to spare at worst; at the run band (207 m in 90 s) or stopping at the
  edges, not. **No timer change proposed** (not clearly needed; what was missing was the way, which the marker now
  shows). Not one continuous run from the golden M to the fort: the bot's steering hit rocks at the first edge in 4 of
  5 walks and a tree in the fifth. If the headset says otherwise, the candidate is the objective's own timer value
  behind a switch (not RE'd: the quest's data, not code seen here).

## 45. The open world's interactions: artifacts and their inspect view, Ithildin glyphs, givers, gates (the collect drill, 2026-10-26)
Headless runs logs/boot-check-20261026-122643 .. -141551 (handoff/HANDOFF-collect.md: the runs, the pictures;
scripts/collect15-drive.sh with collect15_land.py and collect15_walk.py), build 15's switches (headset-build15.env).
No new switch: SOMVR_USE=1 (43.4, on since build 14) already serves the artifact's prompt. Test-only additions: the
words `practice status ground X Y Z` and `practice status look`, the classes in `practice status nav`, the test head's
`pitch`.

### 45.1 Getting there safely: the floor probe and the walk
- `practice status ground X Y Z` (a test word, read only): a ray straight down (PR_RAYCAST's cast, flags 0x50 filter
  0xc) from 30 m over Y to 60 m under it, every surface (6 at most, each ray from 5 cm under the last hit): `PRACTICE
  t=.. ground at (X Y Z): N surface(s) from 30 m over to 60 m under: H (+D m, object O), ...; Talion D m away`. It
  answers from 370 m away (run 122643: the glyph by the sea at 57272 1919 -10603: 2329 and 1709, i.e. a roof 4 m over
  the marker): the world's collision is there far from Talion.
- collect15_land.py: the place's floor (the highest surface at or under the marker + 1 m), then the nearest spot 2.5-6 m
  around (8 bearings, 3 rings) whose top surface (open sky) is within -2.5..+1.5 m of that floor: the trip's target =
  that surface + 40 cm (Teleport snaps down; the arrival wants him within 3 m under the target, 27.7). Every trip of
  the drill arrived after 1 teleport, 0 WARN in all 8 runs. Talion stands 0.5-1 m over the ray's surface on grass and
  rubble (the ray misses some of what he stands on).
- collect15_walk.py: the stick forward, the test head turned to the place (the yaw-to-heading base learnt from a first
  step), slower in the last 3 m, stopping at the first place prompt (not the fight's or the wraith's) or the stop
  distance; `--look Y` pitches the head at the place's height (`head X Y Z [yaw DEG] [pitch DEG] [s SEC]`, the layer's
  test head, somvr_testhead_layer.c: the turn, then the pitch about the turned right axis) and turns it 20/40 deg each
  way.

### 45.2 Artifacts: the prompt needs the wraith vision; B picks; the inspect view's object is not seen
- The three `Collectible_Artifact` markers (34776 2448 -27463 under an arch, 28596 5553 -33884 on a crag top, 61239 980

  try`: **no prompt and no pick** in runs 122643, 123525, 125841 (123 there = the grab's swing `PC_Grab_Attempt_F_Fail`).

## 48. Smoother hands and a weighted sword: `SOMVR_HANDS_SMOOTH`, `SOMVR_SWORD_WEIGHT` (build 15b candidates, 2026-10-26)

The user after build 15 (logs/boot-check-20261026-165456): "Add some smoothing to my hands. Maybe it's just the Quest's
tracking, but it can look a bit jittery. I think it's mainly when holding the sword, since it amplifies how noticeable
shaking is" and "Add some 'weight' to the sword". Handoff: handoff/HANDOFF-feel.md. Both default off.

### 48.1 Where the jitter comes from (the session's logs, the code)
- **Not the timing.** The grips are located on the game thread at the frame's own views time (6.4: `HAND t=` = the
  H4 `time`), the eyes too, and the lead was right: 23 of the 27 sampled `stereo frame` lines show `display-time error`
  0 ms (the others: the first three frames of the stereo stretch, one -11 ms when the lead's median switched 22 -> 11
  ms). The game ran 90 fps (views time steps 11.1 ms). In the first ~4 s after the stereo start (the per-frame H4
  lines) 15 of 299 frames repeated the views' time and 5 % were `+extrapolated`; none of the 102 later samples were.
- **Not the arm solver or the game's animation.** `ARMS lw` every second, the whole session: the animated weapon node
  off the held one 0.0 cm 0 deg, the right hand off the controller-rigid target 0.0 cm, held frames 90 of 90; the
  sword is set on R_Weapon after the solve (`SOMVR_ARMS_LW=held`), our drawn hand on the same grip (33.4).
- **Not two poses for one frame (checked by the new HANDJIT line).** Each frame locates the grips twice at one time:
  phase 2 (the arms: the drawn hands, the drawn sword, the hits' blade R_Weapon) and H4 (the climb, the bow, the slots,
  the verbs, the finishers). What is drawn is what hits (R_Weapon); HANDJIT logs how far the two locates of one time
  differ (the runtime refining its prediction between them) and whether the arms' time ever differs from the eyes'.
- **So: the controller pose itself.** The Quest 2's controller tracking as WiVRn predicts it (the stream's latency plus
  our two-frame lead: ~22 ms at 90 fps on top), and the hand's own tremor, both made visible by the 1 m blade: 0.1 deg
  of grip rotation is 0.2 mm at the knuckles (10 cm) but 1.8 mm at the tip (100.7 cm). The session's HAND lines are one
  a second after the first 30 frames, so they cannot show frame-to-frame rotation noise; frames 1806-1835 (consecutive,
  the hand nearly still) put the grip's position steps within the log's 1 mm resolution, and the runtime's linear
  velocity at 0.01-0.03 m/s. The logged heading of a grip pointing down is ill-conditioned (its 2nd difference 1-5 deg),
  so no rotation number comes from it. **HANDJIT** (below) now logs the real numbers each 10 s of a headset session:
  the next one says how big the noise is at the hand and at the tip, raw and smoothed.

### 48.2 The smoothing: `SOMVR_HANDS_SMOOTH=on` (somvr_smooth.c, pure; somvr_smooth_game.c)
- A One Euro filter per grip, rotation and position apart, in XR space (it commutes with the game's mirror): each frame
  the filtered pose moves toward the located one by alpha = x / (1 + x), x = 2 pi fc dt, the rotation as a slerp.
  fc = MIN + BETA x speed, the speed = the runtime's angular (linear) velocity: the gyro sees a swing's first frame, so
  the cutoff rises at once (without runtime velocities: a finite difference low-passed at 10 Hz).
- Defaults: rotation 1.5 Hz + 12 Hz per rad/s, position 4 Hz + 40 Hz per m/s. A still hand: rotation ~2 Hz (tau 80 ms).
  A swing: the delay of a first-order low-pass on a ramp is tau = 1 / (2 pi fc): 4.2 ms at 3 rad/s (172 deg/s), 2.2 ms
  at 6, 1.3 ms at 10; the angle behind saturates at 1 / (2 pi 12) rad = 0.76 deg (13 mm at the tip) however fast. The
  position: 3.6 ms at 1 m/s.
- Both game-thread locates are filtered (two states, one per locate): the drawn hands, the drawn sword, the hits'
  blade (R_Weapon) and everything that reads H4's grips see the filtered pose; the eyes' views and time are untouched.
- Resets (the raw pose at once, no catch-up glide): a step over 0.1 s, the raw pose 15 cm or 26 deg off the filtered
  one beyond the step's own motion (the runtime's speed x dt: a recentre, tracking regained), an invalid hand. The
  same time again (a repeated views time) = the same pose.

### 48.3 The weight: `SOMVR_SWORD_WEIGHT=light|heavy|on|off` (Blade & Sorcery's feel, not its physics)
- The blade follows the right grip through a critically damped spring-damper on the relative motion: rotation about
  the grip point (a rotation vector) and a little position, each capped. It is driven by the hand's change of speed,
  and only by the part above a gate (smoothstep 1.5..3.5 rad/s, 0.6..1.5 m/s): a still, trembling or slowly moving hand
  gets exactly nothing (no wobble, no lag); a fast swing's start leaves the blade a few degrees behind, its stop lets
  it run on and settle back, never ringing (critically damped, the cap holds the rate outward).
- light (`on`): omega 40/s, at most 3 deg and 0.5 cm; heavy: 26/s, 6 deg, 1 cm. Both hands on the hilt (SOMVR_TWOHAND):
  1.6 x stiffer, the caps / 1.6. test_smooth: an 8 rad/s swing reached in 67 ms trails 3.0 deg (light; 5.7 heavy),
  runs on 3.0 deg at the stop, settles in 133 ms (heavy 256 ms).
- Where: on the right weapon node after `SOMVR_ARMS_LW=held` put it back on the solved hand and before the hits' blade
  is read from R_Weapon, as the node would be if the grip had the blade's pose (`gm2 (x) gm^-1 (x) W`): **the drawn

## 53. The quit: no crash at the game's exit, the end without a Stop, a start while the last session ends (build 16, 2026-10-27)

Build 15b's headset session (logs/boot-check-20261026-233334) ended in a crash when the player quit from the game's
menus, and the session then waited for the PC window's Stop; the session before it (165456) the same. Handoff:
handoff/HANDOFF-launch.md "build 16". Switch: `SOMVR_XR_EXIT=on|off` (layer, default on); the harness parts have no
switch (scripts/boot_check.sh, scripts/som-vr-headset.sh, scripts/somvr_window.py).

### 53.1 The cause
- **The crash.** The game quits with `exit()`: its menus' Quit Game, and its SIGTERM handler (boot_check's stop, so
  also the VR menu's Quit). It never calls vkDestroyDevice, so the layer's session teardown (which joins the watcher,
  36) never runs. The exit handlers run while the watcher thread (36: the gaps, the keep-alive) is still ending frames
  of its own - the game stopped presenting at the confirm, so the keep-alive was on - and the OpenXR loader's static
  destructor (`RuntimeInterface being destroyed`, game.log) dlcloses the runtime. The watcher's next `xrWaitFrame`
  jumps into unmapped code: coredump 1607421 (`#0/#1 n/a`, `#2 xr_wait_publish`, `#3 ka_frame`, `#4 vd_thread` in
  libVkLayer_somvr_openxr.so; the core maps libopenxr_loader.so.1 but no runtime library). Feral's crash handler then
  writes a minidump and starts its reporter and FeralLinuxMessage, a message box nobody can see in the headless
  gamescope: the process stays alive. somvr.log's RATE lines stop ~5 s after the confirm; no END lines (the preload's
  destructor never ran).
- **Not only the headset.** The headless boots of 10-26 18:03-19:08 that ended with boot_check's `quit` (SIGTERM):
  9 of 13 crashed the same way (cores 1468956, 1501384, ...: `xr_wait_publish` / `ka_frame` / `vd_thread`), exit
  137 = SIGKILL after the 30 s grace. Build 9 (no watcher) exited by itself ~2 s after the confirm (10-24, exit 0).
- **The wait after it.** boot_check's stop: `endlogs` (3 s for END lines that never came: the writer thread was
  dead), SIGTERM, then always 30 s for Steam's sync; the launcher noticed the unit's end within 5 s; the PC window
  closed 30 s later; a start before the unit ended was refused ("already running").

### 53.2 The fix in the layer: `SOMVR_XR_EXIT` (somvr_void_layer.c, the code at its end)
- `xr_exit`, an `atexit` handler registered at the first session's start (xe_session from vd_start): after the
  loader's and the runtime's own registrations (they register at xrCreateInstance), so it runs before them (LIFO). It
  takes X.mx (2 s at most: a frame in flight ends first), sets VD.stop and joins the watcher (1 s at most; it never
  waits for X.mx, 36), clears the keep-alive's queue lock (KA.q), stops the preload's xrLocateViews/xrLocateSpace
  (`somvr_xr_stop` -> xr.state DEAD, its calls in flight waited for, 1 s) and leaves every hook pass-through (X.ds NULL,
  phase dead: no frame, no new session, no teardown). Nothing is destroyed: the game did not destroy its device, and
  the runtime's objects end with the process as they did in build 9's clean exit. It logs `xr: exit: the game is
  exiting (...)`: the watcher, the provider, the phase, the frames, the runtime, the time (26-28 ms in the runs).
- The runtime's library is **pinned**: one more `dlopen(RTLD_NOLOAD)` reference from `dladdr(xrWaitFrame)` (unless it
  is the loader's own code), never released - a late call cannot jump into unmapped code. Logged at the session's
  start: `xr: exit: on: ...; the runtime: .../libopenxr_monado.so pinned (never unmapped while the process lives)`.
- `SOMVR_XR_EXIT=off`: build 15b (no handler, no pin; `xr: exit: off (...)`); a bad value = on, logged.
- Tests (tests/test_layer.c, the mock's `MOCKXR_UNLOAD_AT_EXIT=1`: its own exit handler, registered at
  xrCreateInstance like the loader's, marks the runtime unloaded; every XR call after it is counted and a violation):
  `exit-keep` (the keep-alive ending frames, then `exit(0)`: no XR call after the unload, the watcher joined, a present
  after the handlers reaches the driver alone, xr.state DEAD, the log lines), `exit-present` (a render thread
  presenting every 5 ms through the exit: its presents go on, no XR call), `exit-keep-off` (SOMVR_XR_EXIT=off: the
  watcher calls the unloaded runtime - build 15b's crash, reproduced), `void-badcfg` (a bad value). 159/159; the three
  exit scenarios 25 times each without a failure.

### 53.3 The harness: the end by itself (scripts/boot_check.sh)
- **The end watched** (`quit_watch`, from svc every second, so also inside `wait`/`waitlog`): the harness ends the game
  itself with a fast stop when it is still alive 10 s after the layer's exit line (a hang in exit()), 2 s after a crash
  (game.log: `ShadowOfMordor: dumped to "` or `Game crashed with signal` - this run's crash only; Feral's reporter or
  FeralLinuxMessage running counts only once the frames stopped for 3 s, because the game starts its reporter for a
  "previous run" in the middle of normal runs), or after 60 s without a frame once it showed some (somvr.log RATE
  `H9=0`, or no line for 5 s; the sessions' longest H9=0 streak in play was 7 s). The player never needs Stop.
- **The fast stop** (stop_game): no `endlogs`, SIGTERM, 3 s, SIGKILL of the whole tree (the reporter and the box too).
  The player's Stop on a game that already crashed is a fast stop too, and a crash during the normal 30 s grace (build
  15b's SIGTERM -> exit -> crash) = SIGKILL at once.
- **The Steam wait** (`steam_wait`; was 30 s always): done when Steam dropped the game's process (gameprocess_log.txt
  `AppID 241930 no longer tracking PID <game>,` after the launch's offset; or it never tracked it / is not running:
  then no exit sync either), its exit sync ended (cloud_log.txt `Starting sync (up,AC Exit` then
  `YldWriteCacheDirectoryToFile`: every one of the ~400 exit syncs in Steam's logs is that sequence within one second;
  none within 5 s of the drop = none) and remote/ + remotecache.vdf (names, sizes, ns mtimes) stayed unchanged 3 s; at
  most 30 s, then checked anyway (logged). The checks after it are unchanged (GameData.sav byte-compared with the
  pre-launch backup and restored if changed, remotecache.vdf compared, the save guard's lines).
- run.log `the end: N s (the game gone at +a s, the save checked at +b s)`, counted from the cleanup's start.
- Tests: scripts/test_boot_check_end.sh (the functions cut out of boot_check.sh; fake Steam logs and save files,
  stand-in processes: a copy of sleep named FeralLinuxMessage, a game that ignores SIGTERM): 31 checks, ~90 s.

### 53.4 The launcher and the PC window
- **A start while the last session ends** (som-vr-headset.sh `start_gate`): boot_check writes `--ending-file
  $PRIV/ending` when its cleanup starts (the launcher removes it before each start); the unit running with that file,
  or deactivating (the Stop), = ending: a notification ("starting in a moment"), `$PRIV/next-start` (the old PC window
  shows "The last session is closing - the next one starts by itself in a moment."), a wait for the unit's end (at most
  5 min; the unit's TimeoutStopSec is 240) and the normal start. A session playing or starting still refuses ("already
  running"); a dry run never waits. A lock (flock on $RT/somvr-headset.lock) around the unit's start: two starts that
  waited for the same end - the second refuses; the scripts are never copied into $PRIV while a session runs.
- The unit is checked every second (the headset every 5 s), so its end is seen at once; the session's run folder is
  taken while it runs (a next session's folder can be newer by the time this one is reported).
- The PC window closes 10 s after the end (was 30 s), the save check's result shown; its end text says "a few seconds".
- Tests: scripts/test_som_vr_headset_gate.sh (start_gate and session_ending cut out, a fake systemctl): 15 checks.

### 53.5 The headless proof (scripts/headset-build16.env with `SOMVR_XR_EXIT=on`, the test hands, Monado 20 Hz, the build-6 launch to the practice meadow; each 0 WARN in somvr.log and xr-layer.log, the install unchanged, the real save UNCHANGED, remotecache.vdf unchanged, the save guard's writes caught)

| 20261027-002636 | the user's path by keys: pause > QUIT > Yes (to the main menu, the save write) > QUIT GAME > Yes | +1 s | +5 s, exit 0 by itself | +9 s (dropped 0.0 s, sync 0.5 s, steady 3.5 s) | none: no crash line, crashes/ only VersionInfo.txt, no core; END lines by the game's exit |
| 20261027-003052 | the VR menu's Quit (the word `quitgame` at the meadow) -> quit.request -> SIGTERM | +1.2 s | +11 s (SIGTERM +10 s), exit 0 | +14 s | none |
| 20261027-003737 | the user's path, `SOMVR_XR_EXIT=off` (build 15b) | - | the crash at ~+10 s (the minidump line), ended by the harness at +12 s | +16 s | **reproduced**: core 1757770 `xr_wait_publish` / `ka_frame` / `vd_thread` into unmapped code; the fast stop, no Stop |

## 52. The sword's weight, Blade & Sorcery's way: `SOMVR_SWORD_WEIGHT=heavy|light` rebuilt, the VR menu's Sword weight row (build 16 candidate, 2026-10-27)

Session logs/boot-check-20261026-233334 (build 15b, SOMVR_SWORD_WEIGHT=light, SOMVR_HANDS_SMOOTH=on), mark 6 (233820):
the sword needs more weight - one hand could wiggle it freely. Handoff: handoff/HANDOFF-feel.md ("build 16"). Also in
this branch: the merge of t3/build-15b-sword-bow-fixes (46.5: SOMVR_SWORD_GRIP_CM=8, the fist on the handle).

### 52.1 Why light was not felt (the session's SWORDWT lines)
- Light (48.3) only acted above a speed gate (1.5..3.5 rad/s) and capped the blade at 3 deg off the hand (5 cm at the
  1 m tip). In the session's fight (815925-815995) the cap was reached in nearly every window (`capped 76 .. 500`
  sub-frames a window, `the blade off the hand up to 3.00 deg`), 30-60 swing pulses each 10 s: the user's wiggles and
  swings ran at full speed and the blade stayed within 3 deg of the hand - 1:1 to the eye. Nothing in the pipeline
  else: the drawn sword is R_Weapon after the weight (48.3), the hands 1:1.

### 52.2 The model (somvr_smooth.c `swg_*`, pure; tests/test_smooth.c)
Not physics but its feel: the blade's direction d (a unit vector in the grips' space) follows the hand's blade axis
through an acceleration-limited follower; the hand itself is never moved.
- Each frame the hand's turn r = log(q q_prev^-1) is spread over 4 ms sub-steps (exact at 20 Hz too). Per sub-step the
  blade's angular speed w_b chases the target `w_hand (its swing part: no twist about d) + k e` (e = the turn from d
  to the hand's axis, k = omega / (2 zeta)) at the rate 2 zeta omega, within limits: the part of the change that slows
  the blade at a_dn (400 rad/s^2, down to a stop), everything else - speeding up, turning to a new direction, a
  reversal's far side - at a_up. From rope0 off the hand that limit grows (to 4 a_dn at rope: the rope "stretches");
  at rope the blade is held (no speed away from the hand). |w_b| <= w_max (20 rad/s; both hands 30).
- So: a slow cut (under a_up) is 1:1; a fast one leaves the blade behind until the stretch pulls it along, and it
  catches up after the stop without running past (a_dn); a quick wiggle's reversals need far more than a_up, so the
  blade only swings a part of it; the twist about the blade (the edge's turn, a roll of the wrist) is the hand's.
- Heavy: a_up 24 rad/s^2, omega 25/s, zeta 2.7 (the pull 4.6/s), rope0 9 deg, rope 16 deg. Light: a_up 60, omega 30,
  rope0 5, rope 9. Both hands on the hilt (SOMVR_TWOHAND): the limits x 4.6^2, the loop x 4.6, the ropes / 4.6 (heavy
  3.5 deg), w_max x 1.5; a rope that shrinks (the left hand takes the hilt) closes at 86 deg/s, no jump.
- Resets (the blade on the hand at once): a gap over 0.1 s, a 34+ deg step faster than 40 rad/s, a NaN; none while
  SOMVR_HANDS_SURFACE holds the hand, with the bow, without a sword (as 48.3).

### 52.3 The numbers (tests/test_smooth.c, 90 Hz, a 9 Hz tremor of 0.1 deg and 0.05 deg noise per axis; the blade at SOMVR_SWORD_ANGLE 20)
Cuts are minimum-jerk (the shape of a human reach); wiggles sines; "lag" = the blade's largest angle off the hand,
"settled" = after the hand stops until it stays within 1 deg, "share" = the blade's swing / the hand's (the middle 0.6 s).

| motion | heavy, one hand | light, one hand | heavy, two hands |
|---|---|---|---|
| slow cut 60 deg in 0.8 s (2.5 rad/s) | lag 0.6 deg, settled 0 ms | 0.6 deg | 0.5 deg |
| cut 90 deg in 0.35 s (8.4 rad/s) | lag 11.2 deg, settled 106 ms | 4.3 deg, 0 ms | 1.6 deg |
| fast cut 120 deg in 0.25 s (15.7 rad/s) | lag 13.5 deg, settled 117 ms | 6.6 deg, 50 ms | 2.8 deg, 17 ms |
| flick 90 deg in 0.15 s (19.5 rad/s) | lag 15.6 deg, settled 283 ms | 8.5 deg, 28 ms | 2.9 deg, 39 ms |
| wiggle +-10 deg at 5 Hz | 32 % (off up to 8.6 deg) | 69 % | 107 % |
| wiggle +-15 deg at 4 Hz | 45 % | 82 % | 105 % |
| wiggle +-20 deg at 3 Hz | 68 % | 92 % | 104 % |
| wiggle +-25 deg at 2 Hz | 83 % | 102 % | 102 % |
| roll 90 deg in 0.2 s (about the blade) | 0.00 deg (no noise) | 0.00 | - |

Every case: no run-on past the hand over 2 deg (heavy 0.0-0.5), within the rope, the blade's speed within its cap,
nothing added by the tremor before the motion (under 0.25 deg), no twist off the hand, at most 8 deg of change of the
offset in one frame (a 19.5 rad/s flick moves the hand 12 deg a frame). 20 Hz (the headless runtime): the fast cut
lags 12.2 deg (90 Hz 13.5). The left hand taking the hilt mid-cut: no jump (4.19 deg in a frame, as one hand).

### 52.4 Haptics
- The drag: a pulse on the sword hand when the blade falls 0.6 x rope0 behind (heavy 5.4 deg, light 3) while the hand
  turns at 3+ rad/s: heavy 0.4 .. 0.7 (the faster, the stronger), light 0.25 .. 0.4, 70 ms; both hands: 0.7 x on the
  right, 0.5 x on the left; re-armed when the blade is back within half that, at most one each 0.3 s (a wiggle is no
  buzz).
- The controller blade's hits: full strength, heavy 2 x as long (light 1.5 x, as 48.3); both hands on the hilt: the
  left hand 0.6 for as long. The defence's and the execution's pulses unchanged.

### 52.5 What the hits read (for the combat helper's weak/strong mapping; nothing of the classification changed)
- The drawn sword is the hits' blade: the weight is set on R_Weapon (swg_arm, after SOMVR_ARMS_LW=held and before
  `g_arm.wpn` is taken), and SOMVR_BLADE=controller's grip is that node's (arm_blade_grip: `X (x) R_Weapon (x)
  CAL_R^-1`), so `somvr_blade` base/tip are the drawn blade's.
- Its speed: with SOMVR_BLADE_VEL unset (build 16), `vel_tip` is the finite difference of that tip in tracking space
  (somvr_blade_controller), i.e. the drawn (weighted) blade's speed - a wiggle the blade absorbs is slower at the tip,
  a fast cut's blade reaches about the hand's peak a little later. The tier (sc_tier: slash 3 m/s and 15 cm, heavy 6 m/s
  and 40 cm, stab along the blade) reads `g_cb.sp` (its mean over 80 ms) of those tips.
- The defence's contact and the clank read the same blade (`g_cb.prev` -> `g_df.bb/bt`); contact_move_cm reads the
  sword hand's grip (the hand, 1:1).
- Logged per 10 s: `SWORDWT ... the blade off the hand up to D deg (at the rope N sub-steps); the swing speed up to H
  rad/s, the blade's B; drag pulses, hits`.

### 52.6 The VR menu's Sword weight row (somvr_vrmenu.c/.h)
- settings byte 79 (`sword_weight`, was pad3: no version change; 80 bytes), key `SWORD_WEIGHT` = the switch

- Tests: test_vrmenu (the key, the byte, put/get/file, the row's place, shown/enabled, the values, the steps, its >

### 52.7 Switches, words, lines
| Switch | Default | What |

## 49. Y always lets go of the wraith vision; the wraith's copy of the held sword: `SOMVR_VISION`, `SOMVR_HP_COPIES` (build 16, 2026-10-27)

Build 15b's headset session (logs/boot-check-20261026-233334, marks 9-11) ended in the wraith vision with no way
out, and with a see-through second sword beside the held one (mark 9's eyes: two swords side by side, one a glassy
copy). Handoff: handoff/HANDOFF-wraith.md, "build 16"; driver scripts/wraith16-drive.sh.

### 49.1 Why Y could not turn it off **[high]**
- somvr.log: `VISION t=816028.460 Y pressed: a tap of 122 ... (the vision off -> on)`, `816028.761 the wraith vision on
  (flag 1)`, then no `Y let go` line and no later VISION line at all: build 15b's hold mode turned the vision off only
  on a release while it was "ours", and a press with the vision on did nothing - so once the release was lost, no
  button could end it.
- How the release was lost: `SOMVR_MARK=1`'s chord (28: B + Y held together = a bug mark) holds every Y press back
  `window_s` = 0.12 s to see whether B joins it; a press let go within that window reaches the controls as one press
  with the button already up - somvr_ctl's "a tap shorter than a tick: down for this one" - so the game side sees Y
  for exactly one input tick. go_vision_tick took the press (the on tap, 2 ticks) and saw the release on the next
  tick, while its tap still ran (`tap && !vis_tap`: the off was dropped without a line) and the flag still read 0 (the
  game turns it ~50 ms after the tap): `vis_ours` cleared, no off. Then the on landed. tests/test_vision.c's chain test
  runs the raw Y through the real chord (somvr_session.c) and controls (somvr_ctl.c): a 40 ms press = 1 tick at the
  game side.
- Not the wrist panel: the layer opened it by the palm gesture 312 ms after the press (`vrmenu: opened by the palm
  gesture`, `SURF ... the wrist panel is open`), but the panel takes only the right trigger from the game (`consume`),
  never Y, and the context stayed `world`.
- The session's first quick press (815727.933 on, .991 off "refused") is the game's own dwell (49.2): the off came
  58 ms after the on.

### 49.2 The game's toggle, measured (run 20261027-002021, the word `vision taps N MS`) **[high]**
PC_WraithPing on CombatSecondary01 (122) answers ~50 ms after the tap's first tick (20 Hz headless frames), and keeps
each state at least ~1 s:
- off -> on -> a second tap 60 ms after the on: dropped (the vision stays on); an off tap 0.40 s and 0.75 s after an on:
  dropped; 1.05 s after: lands 50 ms later.
- on -> off -> a second tap 150, 250, 400, 700 ms after: **held back, not dropped** - it lands 1.003, 1.003, 1.002,
  1.05 s after the off; 1000 ms after: lands 50 ms later.
So a tap inside the dwell either vanishes or lands late, and a retry on top of a held-back tap could toggle twice.

### 49.3 What is built: Y's wish (somvr_vision.c, pure; game side somvr_gameopts_game.c)
- Y gives a wish and taps bring the flag (`PlayerVisionMode+0x48`, read as the step module reads it) to it.
  - hold (build 16's env, as 15b's): a press with the vision off - or going off, or an off still wished - wishes it on
    and makes it ours; **Y not held while it is ours wishes it off** (the level each tick, not the release's edge: a
    release the game side never saw cannot leave it on); **a press with the vision on (the game's own, a phase's
    look, a story moment) wishes it off**.
  - tap: a press = the other state.
- A tap: 2 input ticks of 122 (allow_cmd past the deny list, as before), a tick without the command before the next
  one. It starts only in the world and only **1.05 s after the flag's last change** (the dwell, 49.2): the off of a
  quick press waits for its on and the dwell (the vision shows ~1.1 s at least, the game's own minimum); an on right
  after an off waits too, so the game never holds one back. A tap not answered within 0.3 s is tapped again, 6 taps at
  most, then given up with a line (the next press tries again). A change nobody tapped for is the game's own: no wish,
  left alone until Y. The flag unread: build 15b's blind edges (a tap on the press, one on the release).
- Lines: every change of the flag (`VISION t=.. the flag 0 -> 1: our tap's, 50 ms after it` or `no tap of ours
  waiting`), every wish, tap, retry, `as wished (N ms, K taps)`, `NOT reached ... given up`; `VISION END` counts.
- Test words: `vision` (a state line), `vision y MS` (Y held MS ms at the snapshot, before the chord; 1 = the
  shortest press), `vision taps N MS` (N raw taps, no wish of ours).
- No new switch: `SOMVR_VISION=hold|tap` (default unset = off, build 9's 243) keeps its words; its hold mode is fixed.
  tests/test_vision.c (39 checks) against a simulated toggle with the measured dwell: hold, the quick press (1 and 12
  ticks), a 0.5 s hold, a press with the vision on (ours let go and pressed again, the game's own), the game turning it
  on and off by itself, a refusing game (6 taps, given up, the next press works), the flag unread, tap mode, menus,
  and the chord chain; with a 0.35 s spacing instead of 1.05 s, 10 checks fail (taps dropped and held back).
